text:
I have always been interested in studying living creatures and following their behaviour. Those small, winged friends of ours in particular have always delighted me. Their colourful displays and their many different sounds have been with me since childhood.

When I lived in the city, their busier way of life was clearly different from what I have experienced since we moved. Now that I live in a quieter area, I have been able to study and admire them more closely. Their many sounds have always been there: singing, display calls and all sorts of other things.

In the city the noise of all the traffic easily covered their sounds, but here their song is heard clearly. That has been a real delight, because it brings a lot of joy and closeness to nature into my everyday life.

I have had the pleasure of growing up in the peace of the countryside, where mornings begin to the accompaniment of song. Memories of childhood summers in particular are close to my heart. Back when the world felt much larger and every day was an adventure. I remember sitting in the yard and listening as the sounds drifting through the air told their own stories.

When I walked along the paths that wound around the edge of the field, I felt myself part of something greater. Every step revealed new views: the shades of the flowers, the secrets of the leaves in the grove, and the sounds of living nature. Silence was present everywhere, but it was not empty space - it was full of life, which revealed itself slowly to those who took the trouble to listen.

Those times taught me to value detail and an unhurried pace. The peace of the countryside has stayed with me forever, and it has given me strength and inspiration to face all of life's challenges. Even though life has carried me into the heart of the city, that childhood landscape remains in my heart, always reminding me of what really matters.

I have always been attached to the calm atmosphere of the countryside. I grew up in a place where I could enjoy the morning sun and watch the birds dance in the sky. These animals have been a passion and a pastime for me. Being interested in birds, I have learned to recognise their calls and to follow their behaviour.

When I lived in the city, I noticed how different the atmosphere is there. The noise, the lights, the clamour of people, all of it seemed to muddle my mind and make me anxious. But then I found a place of my own in the city - a park where I could escape the noise and listen to birdsong. For me it was like a little piece of the countryside there in the middle of the concrete forest.

The most beautiful thing about nature is how it can bring peace and balance into a life. When I sit in the park and listen to the birds singing, I feel myself released from all worries and troubles. For me it is like a breathing hole that gives me strength and inspiration for everyday life.

I have always been enchanted by the diversity of life. I grew up in the countryside, where mornings were full of sparrows singing in the trees and in the evenings you could hear swallows crying from the sky. Those sounds are still familiar and often come to mind.

Living in the city, I have noticed that although the noise is of a different kind, the sounds of nature find their way through. For example, when walking in the park I often notice birds singing in the bushes. It is wonderfully calming.

Nature and its forms of life have always been important to me. They remind me that there is far more in the world than just the environment people have made. Every moment when I can get away from the rush of the city and get to know the variety of nature is valuable time for me.

Interviewer: How have you experienced the effects of the changes in your surroundings recently?

Guest: I have noticed that when I lived in the countryside as a child, I often woke early in the morning to the accompaniment of beautiful songs. Now, living in the city, I often wake to the noise of traffic. For me that has been like a piece taken out of my soul. The beauty and peace I experienced in the sounds of nature have been exchanged for the rumble of machines and the din of the marketplace.

Interviewer: Do you have favourite animals that have been close to you?

Guest: Yes, I have always been especially interested in those small, quick-moving creatures you see gliding in the sky. Their appearance in the morning outside my window has always brought a smile to my face. Their presence and their beauty have given me a great deal of comfort and peace.

Interviewer: How does nature affect you these days?

Guest: Even though I am mostly in the city now, I try to look for closeness to nature in parks and small green areas. They are like tiny oases in the middle of concrete and asphalt. Their sounds, a glance up into a tree, or watching those wings glide through the air, give me a feeling of release and calm. It is like a piece of home, back to the landscapes of my childhood.

I have always been enchanted by the calm of forests and field valleys. In summer I often wake early, having heard bright, cheerful sounds ring in through my window. They are like little messages from the world outside, and they invite me out to explore the surrounding nature.

When I walk through green parks or old forests, every step reveals new sights and sounds. The winds whisper secrets to the leaves, and sometimes I catch sight of a quickly flitting wing or a sharp eye watching me with interest. Even in the middle of cities there are places where you can hear that magical melody. It is as though you were part of a wider symphony being played around the clock.

Every time I leave the noise of the city and move into calmer surroundings, I feel refreshed again. The cleansing effect of the air, the warmth of the sun against my skin and all these sounds together create an experience that is both relaxing and inspiring. It is like returning to being part of something wider and more ancient, whose existence does not depend on human affairs.

When I was a child, I loved spending time at my parents' cabin. It was in a remote place where the sounds of nature were almost the only sounds you could hear. I remember the mornings especially, when countless different birds sang in the sky. Their songs blended together beautifully with the calm mood of nature.

When I grew up and later moved to a larger city, I noticed that I missed the peace of the cabin. In the city the noise and clamour were constantly present, and it was not easy to find places where you could enjoy the same stillness as at the cabin. Still, every now and then, when I walked in parks or green areas, I caught a glimpse of the peace I had learned to value in the lap of nature in childhood. The birds were still there, singing beautiful melodies that gave me the feeling that some of that childhood magic was still with me.

Even though my life has moved on and I have settled into a new environment, the memories of the calm days at the cabin and the beautiful songs of the birds have remained very valuable to me. They remind me how important it is to find a balance between the rush of the city and the peace of nature.

I have always been especially interested in life in the countryside. I love how the sunlight dapples through the trees and creates cool shade in the middle of the day. And the sounds! They are so different from the city. Here you can hear even the smallest animals moving in the bushes and the trees. In the mornings especially it is perfect to sit outside and listen... to those small creatures that wake first.

When I have walked in the forests, I have often wondered how they manage to communicate with each other in so many different ways. They can warn each other of danger and call each other to feed. It really is astonishing. In the city it is easy to think that it is all just concrete and asphalt, but here in the middle of nature you realise how much life there is everywhere - on the branches of trees, in the bushes, even on the roof. And all these sounds! It is like a style of music of its own that you cannot hear anywhere else.

Here in the middle of nature you can also notice how the times of day affect the lives of the animals. Mornings and evenings are always especially active times... for those small creatures. In the city you might not pay attention to how daylight affects the world around you, but here it is part of everyday life. And it is something I always miss whenever I am away from here.

I have always been particularly fond of birdwatching in the summer. The calm surroundings of the countryside offer an ideal place for this hobby. Mornings are especially important to me, because they offer the chance to hear the beautiful songs of the birds and to observe their colourful feathers.

When I sit outside at sunrise, there are only the sounds of nature around me. The wind stirs the leaves in the trees, and from a distance you can hear the splash of the rivers. This calm mood creates the perfect opportunity to concentrate on watching the birds and to enjoy the beauty of the surrounding nature.

I particularly remember one occasion when I got to see a rare species. I had sat for many hours waiting, and finally it appeared. Its feathers were a beautiful blue, and its song was like nothing I had heard before. That experience strengthened my enthusiasm for birdwatching and underlined for me the importance of the diversity of nature.

Moments like these are very important to me, because they give me the chance to escape everyday life and to experience something truly unique. The calm of the countryside and the beauty of nature offer the perfect combination, which inspires me to continue watching birds and to value nature even more.

I have always been enchanted by the diversity of life around us. I remember from my childhood walking through forests and fields, listening to the song of those small, quick-moving creatures whose sounds filled the air. They were like nature's own instruments, conjuring peace and balance into my heart.

As I grew older, I noticed that the presence of these animals was not only in the countryside but also close to us, even in the centres of cities. Their sounds mixed with the passing of cars and the talk of people, but they still kept their own character and their calming effect. They reminded me that nature is present everywhere, even when we do not always notice it.

When I sit on my balcony in the heart of the city, I still hear those familiar sounds. They are like greetings from friends, reminding me of the beauty and diversity of life. Even though the surrounding world can be noisy and hurried, with the help of these sounds I can find a moment of peace and connection with nature.

I have always been especially fond of remote places where you can hear only the message of the wind and the sounds of animals. Last summer I spent several nights in a farmhouse that stood on the top of a high hill. At night when I went outside, the sky was full of light, and in the yard I felt I was part of something greater. When I woke in the morning I heard birdsong behind the window; it was so beautiful that I almost cried. The silence and the peace there were something I had never experienced before. It really was a wonderful experience.

I have always been enchanted by the calm of the countryside. Last summer I spent several weeks at my parents' farm, which was quite far from the city. In the mornings I always woke early to the songs of the birds. It felt as though the whole world had come alive around me.

When I walked in the field or in the forest, you really had to concentrate to be able to tell apart all those different sounds. Some birds sing at such a high pitch that it almost hurts the ear. Others make lower, more rhythmic sounds. It was like nature's own symphony.

Living in the city, I have never paid as much attention to those sounds. There is so much human-made noise there that nature's own sounds cannot come through. But there in the countryside, far from the din of the city, you could hear every bird's song clearly and feel yourself part of that great, living whole.

I have always felt at home here in the country. I still remember from my childhood walking along the paths with my grandparents and listening to their stories about the history and the secrets of this area. One place in particular has stayed in my mind - an old, magnificent oak, under which we often sat and watched the animals.

I remember my grandfather teaching me the sounds of the different species. He said that if you know how to listen properly, you can notice many things around you. And he was right - when you sat there in the silence and concentrated, you began to notice everything: birdsong, the rustle of leaves, the echoes of the trees... It was like a world of its own opening up in front of your eyes.

As I grew up, I have often returned to that place. Nowadays it is part of my own traditions - whenever I need peace or am looking for inspiration, I go and sit there and listen. It is a place where time seems to stop, and the rush and noise of the world fade into the background. And although the years have rolled by, that oak is still there, a steady reminder of times past and of the things learned there - of silence, of the beauty of nature and of the secrets of life.

I have always been drawn to the edges of the forest, where the trees and bushes offer a sheltered place for many animals. One day I was sitting with some birdwatchers waiting for the birds to arrive, when suddenly there was a strange, high sound. It made us all look around and wonder what could have caused it.

A moment later we saw a small, colourful bird land near us. It was still singing that same melody that had astonished us at first. It was a truly beautiful and rare bird, and seeing it was a great joy for us.

When we are in the city, the sounds are often louder and more varied than in nature. The hum of buses, the talk of people and sirens create a noisy environment that can be both disturbing and energising.

Somewhere deep inside me, though, there has always been a certain pull towards calmer places, where the sounds of nature can take over the space. Perhaps that is the reason why parks and forests have always been so important to me; they offer an opportunity to escape the noise of the city and to swim among those other sounds.

The interviewer sat comfortably on a bench at the edge of the park and turned to look at the person being interviewed. "Tell us a little about your experiences in the middle of this beautiful environment," she asked with a smile.

The interviewee smiled broadly and began to speak: "I have always been enchanted by how many different sounds the birds of this place can produce. Some are so high and sharp that they almost break in the air, while others are soft and melodic. It is as if they had a language of their own that they speak to each other." He glanced up into the treetops, where a group of sparrows was visible on the branches.

"What do you find yourself thinking when you hear these sounds?" the interviewer asked curiously. The interviewee closed his eyes and breathed deeply. "It takes me back to my childhood, when I lived in the countryside. In the mornings I woke to the song of the birds, and it was as though the whole world were singing to me. It was calm, but at the same time it gave me energy and enthusiasm to face a new day." He opened his eyes and looked at the interviewer. "This place is a little like that. Even though we are close to the city, here you can still hear the sounds of nature clearly."

When I sat with him on a bench in the green park, he told me how often he seeks peace in the local park. "Here it is possible to forget the rush and noise of everyday life," he said with a smile. He mentioned in particular how the living sounds of the forest comfort him. He found the song of the birds especially pleasing.

He said he often walks in the park and observes the birds that live there. Their colour and variety had enchanted him. "Every day is a new adventure," he grinned, "because I can never know what new species the park will offer me."

When he spoke about the noise of the city, he said that it does not bother him when he is in the park. He explained that nature's own sounds - the rustle of leaves, birdsong and the audible background hum of the forest's rhythms of life - effectively cover the din of the city.

I have always been enchanted by the beauty and diversity of living creatures. Living in the countryside, I have been able to admire different species that you would not necessarily meet in everyday life. Silence is sometimes almost powerful - you only hear it when everything else falls quiet.

I know a person who has spent his whole life studying these refined creatures. Having learned to know their behaviour, he can tell their species apart on the basis of sound alone. According to him, every species has a unique "language" with which they communicate with each other and with nature.

Silence is important, because it lets us listen carefully to sounds that would otherwise go unnoticed. It is also an essential part of the experience when we want to understand life at nature's own pace.

I spent my childhood on my parents' farm, which lay in a quiet valley. I remember how in the mornings I woke to the sound of birdsong and went out into the yard to see which birds had come to visit our yard. Finches, chaffinches, great tits... each sang its own unique melody. It was always so beautiful and calming.

As I grew up, I learned the sounds of the different birds and also taught my brother and sister to recognise them. We spent hours by the yard fence waiting for some rare visitor to come and greet us. And when one appeared, it was always a great joy. The calm and the silence of the countryside gave us the chance to hear and watch birds in a completely different way than would have been possible in the city.

In winter, when the snow cover was at its thickest, we used to go on trips into the forest. Then the world seemed even calmer, and every step pressed the snow down into the lower layers. We looked for the tracks of birds in the snow and tried to guess who had been visiting the trees or the bushes. Those were such wonderful moments, full of a sense of adventure and of togetherness with the family.

Although I have now moved to the city, those experiences have stayed with me. Because of them I understand how important it is to keep a connection with nature and its beauty. And even though birdsong is no longer my alarm clock every morning, I know that it is always there waiting, ready to delight a listener in the peace of the countryside.

I have always been enchanted by how we live in this fine city, which is full of bustle and activity. But when I go to the park, I am always amazed by how much life there is there - those small creatures that fly from tree to tree, singing so beautifully. They produce music that I cannot hear anywhere else.

When I am outside, I feel connected to the world in a way that is hard to explain. It is as though there were something deeper and more meaningful than everything else that happens in this large city. And when I return to my flat, which is near the park, I hear their sounds through my window and it feels so refreshing and calming.

All my life I have been interested in those small fliers that are always in motion. I have tried to learn more about their lives and about how they adapt to this rapidly changing world of ours. It has been a real passion for me, and one that has given me a lot of joy and knowledge.

I have always been attached to the soundscape of forests and farmland. I remember from my childhood how we went to the countryside with my family on summer holiday and woke in the mornings to birdsong. It was like an orchestra of its own, playing to celebrate our waking.

Living in the city, sounds of this kind are rare, but every now and then when I can get out of the concrete environment and visit parks or nearby natural areas, I feel connected to nature again. Birds have always been a particular joy to me - their colouring, their shapes and of course their songs. They bring life even into the middle of the city, when they build their nests on a roof or flit about in the bushes of the parks.

One day I sat in the park and listened carefully to the soundscape spreading around me. The birds were singing, the leaves were rustling in the wind, and somewhere further off you could hear the receding noise of the city - car sirens, the talk of people and the rumble of buses. It was like the backing chorus of a living painting, reminding me that even though we are city dwellers, nature is always present, waiting for us to find it among us.

The interviewee sits in a sunny spot at the edge of the park. She tells me that her childhood family lived in the countryside, where they had a large garden full of different plants and animals. She particularly remembers the almost soundless silence of the morning hour, broken suddenly by a burst of birdsong. She also speaks about how nature made her feel part of a greater whole.

When she moved to the city to study, she began to notice that she missed the peace of the countryside. In the city life was faster and louder. She says she often walks in the park so that she can hear the birds sing. The sounds of the birds are calming music to her, helping her to relax.

The interviewer asks her what she thinks about the fact that city life involves so many different sounds. She answers that sometimes it can be disturbing, but that in general she has learned to adapt to it and to look for the sounds of nature in the city as well.

When I sat with her in the old garden, where the flowering apple trees glowed in the strength of the spring light, she began to talk about her life in the countryside. She told me how, on waking in the mornings, the first thing she heard was the sound of the birds. Their songs were like music that filled the air and made her feel part of a greater whole.

The silence of the countryside was something she had grown used to and even come to love. It gave her space to think and to feel life at a deeper level. And then there were the moments when she sat in the garden, watching the birds that flew from tree to tree or looked for food on the ground. Those moments were full of peace and balance.

As the conversation went on, she mentioned how nature had always been her refuge. The place where she escaped the noise and rush of the city. The sounds of nature, such as the rustle of leaves in the wind or the sound of the trees swaying, were in her view music that made her relax and forget the worries of everyday life.

Finally, as the interview drew to a close, she looked around the garden and said that this place, this silence and these sounds were what she valued most in her life. It was her home, her peace, and the place where she felt she was truly herself.

I have always particularly liked living here in the countryside. In the mornings I often wake early and go out into the yard to listen... to their sounds, which delight my heart again and again. Their song is like music to the ears. Hardly any cars come here, and there is not much other noise either. Even though it sometimes feels as if everything is too quiet and too empty, their presence makes this place homely and safe.

When I am out walking, I often notice them in the trees or in the fields. They are so free and cheerful that it always puts me in a good mood. Here you can also easily notice how the seasons change and how they affect... life in general. In winter it is really beautiful, when the snow covers the landscape in a white cloak and... the sounds are especially clear without the rustle of leaves. In summer, on the other hand, it is wonderfully warm and there is life everywhere.

I know that not everyone necessarily values this calm life the way I do, but for me it is an essential part of my existence. It gives me the chance to concentrate on my own thoughts and feelings and to enjoy the beauty around me without distractions. And when there is so much... life around, it makes this place an even more attractive place for me to live.

I have always been attached to a calm life. I grew up in the countryside as a child, where the air quality was clean and the landscapes were green. I still remember how I woke early in the mornings to the accompaniment of birdsong. Those moments were full of peace and balance.

As I have spent more time in the middle of nature, I have begun to notice all sorts of details that you do not necessarily see at first glance. For example, the way the forest comes alive in spring is always a wonder - when the trees burst into bloom and the birds return to nest, it is as though the whole world wakes up. The silence of the countryside has also taught me to value the simple things in life. It leaves room for reflection and for thinking about oneself in a way that is not necessarily possible in the rush of the city.

Even though life has also taken me to cities, that connection with nature has always stayed in my heart. It is a place I can always return to in search of peace and balance in the middle of life's hurry.

I have always been enchanted by the way the forests and farmlands come alive in spring. When the silence of winter fades, a new generation of singers appears. It feels as though their cheerful composition came straight from the heart. The early morning in particular is the time when the world seems to be in their possession.

Even in the middle of cities you can sometimes hear the echoes of this distant serenade. It gives a flash of what is happening at the edges, where the beauty of nature is still present. I often wonder what it would be like to live closer to the centre of these living olympuses, where every morning and evening brings a new concert.

Silence matters too. How often does the din of the city cover that quiet sound, which can be as beautiful as the song of a bird? Although I live in the city, I always try to find a moment when I can break away from it and let myself soak up nature's own sounds. Every trip to the countryside or to a park is a reminder of how much we still have to learn from life and from its diversity.

I have always been enchanted by the diversity of life. When I sit in the park or even in my own back yard, I notice how many different "singers" there are around me. Some of them are a real joy to the ears - they produce vocal exercises you could not hear at any concert! Others give a slightly different view of what is happening in city life: when their song is smothered under the noise, it is as if it were a sign that we should get away from the racket now and then and seek out calmer places. And then there are the mornings when everything is still quieter - then it feels as though nature itself were speaking to us in its own voice.

I have always been attached to remote areas, where you can hear different sounds and feel a stronger connection with nature. In summer, when the days are long, I often wake before sunrise and go out to listen to the silence of the morning.

It is an especially beautiful time, when the sun rises slowly into the sky and lights up the landscape. I hear many sounds then: birds singing in the trees, and the wind moving through the leaves. It is as though the whole world were awake, and yet everything is so calm.

When I lived in the country as a child, I learned to know many birdsongs. I remember how my father taught me to tell the different species apart by their sounds. It was wonderful, because it made me interested in the world around me and in its many secrets.

Now that I am older, I value more than ever the calm that remote places offer. They give me the chance to stop and to look at the world from a new point of view.

I have always been enchanted by the diversity of life, and especially by how even our smallest creatures can bring joy into everyday life. I remember from my childhood spending a lot of time in the yard watching those feathered friends of ours that came to visit our garden.

Their song was like music to the ears. Every morning, as the sun rose, beautiful melodic sounds drifted through the air. It was like a symphony in which every bird played its own particular part. Even though I lived in the city, that did not stop me enjoying the pleasures nature offered.

As I grew older, I began to understand better and better how important it was to preserve the sound world of nature. The noise and clamour of the city can easily cover those beautiful sounds that are so important to us. That is why I have always tried to do my part so that these small friends of ours can go on enjoying their lives and singing with a full heart.

With my children we have also built a bird feeder in the yard, where they can watch the birds from close up. It has been a very rewarding experience for us all, and it has taught my children to value nature and its inhabitants.

I have always been attached to a calm life in the countryside. I still remember from my childhood how I woke early in the mornings and went out into the yard to listen... to those small creatures full of life that sing so beautifully. Their sounds have always been like music to my ears.

When I sit now in my own yard, there is nothing around me but peace and silence, and every now and then some... winged visitor flies past me. It is just as if the world had stopped, and I am part of that beauty. Everything is so harmonious, and I do not need to hear anything but... nature's own sounds.

This place where I live is like paradise to me. Nobody disturbs me, and I can just sit and watch... the birds playing in the air or looking for food on the ground. It is just as if I were part of their world, and I do not need to worry about anything. Everything is so simple and calm here.

When I sat on the terrace of the old house, the sun shone on the leaves and the birds sang brightly. A quiet evening came down and carried all the din away with it. Nobody spoke, only the sounds of nature filled the air. The birds were so calm, their song was clearly audible. Somewhere in the distance tall trees stood out against the horizon.

Nature was at its most beautiful when it gave us space and a silence that we could not find anywhere else. The birds flew above, and the flashes of their wings were clearly audible. Around us there was only the peace of the countryside, and no din at all could be heard. We were all completely silent, so that we could hear the birds' beautiful sounds and enjoy the beauty of nature.

The interviewer sat opposite me and asked what inspires me most in my everyday life. I looked out of the window and saw a distant park, in the middle of which a group of colourful creatures were on the wing, creatures I have always admired for their beautiful songs.

"For me the most important thing has always been how those little birds can create such a calming mood," I said. "They do not care where they live - whether it is the centre or a park on the edge of town. They are always there, producing music that is completely in a class of its own."

The interviewer nodded with interest and asked whether I had a favourite place where I often went to listen to those creatures. I thought for a moment before answering.

"There is one place," I began. "It is an old park with a busy street running along its edge. Even though the noise of the traffic is almost constant, in the middle of all that din there is a particular calm. I hear their sounds more clearly there than anywhere else, and I find that truly remarkable."

The interviewer smiled and made notes. "And how do these... sounds affect you? Is there something special in them that inspires you?" she asked.

"I think it is the way they can shape the space around them in their own way," I answered. "They do not try to compete with the noise of the city but find their own place in the middle of it. I find that an instructive experience, and it inspires me to look for my own space in the world."

The interviewer nodded contentedly and thanked me for such an open and thoughtful answer.

I have always been attached to life in the countryside, where you can enjoy calm and beauty. In the mornings I often wake to the accompaniment of birdsong, which is a real joy for me. Birds have always been close to me, and I have spent hours watching their lives in my garden. The silence of the countryside has also given me the chance to concentrate on myself and to find inner peace.

When I go outdoors, I often notice how nature speaks in its own voice. The leaves poured out by the wind, the birdsong and the warmth of the sun against my skin - all of this creates a connection that is deep and satisfying. The calm of the countryside gives me the chance to live in the moment and to enjoy the details we often pass by in our hurry.

I have always been enchanted by the sounds of living creatures. In the mornings especially, when I can get away from the middle of the rush and out to the park near my home, I hear many interesting sounds. One of my favourites is to listen early in the morning to how the different singers wake the day.

One morning, when I was walking in the park, I realised how varied these sounds are. Some were beautiful enough to caress the ear and others were a little rougher, but in any case they created a perfect tune that made me feel part of the world around me. Although I have lived for years near a busy street, I have never lost that wonderful feeling these sounds awaken in me.

Once I moved my flat a little further from the centre and noticed how much more life there was around me. The trees were taller, and the "friends" sitting on their branches sang from the heart. It was a truly wonderful experience, which made me value even more the beauty these sounds bring into my life.

In this environment, where nature and the world made by people meet, it is really easy to find a balance. Even though the rush and noise of city life are close by, they have never driven away the peace that listening to these sounds gives me.

I have always been particularly attached to animals that can fly in the sky. Their freedom has always inspired me. Growing up in the city did not offer many opportunities to see them, but when I have spent time in the countryside instead, I have noticed how they fly from tree to tree or sit in the shade singing beautiful melodies. Their sounds are like music to my ears.

One particular experience of mine was when I lived for a while in the countryside and woke every morning early to the beautiful songs of these birds. It was so calming that I have never forgotten the feeling. Even though I have returned to the city, I always try to find opportunities to get away from it and to come back to nature, where these small creatures fly freely. Their presence reminds me of the simplicity and beauty of life.

I have always been enchanted by the diversity of life that can be seen around us. The moments I have spent near water or in forests in particular have given me a deep connection with all living things. Mornings when the sky is full of their beautiful songs have been especially significant for me.

In the middle of cities it is easy to forget how much life and how many sounds there are around us. But when you step away from the noise of the traffic and the glare of the concrete surface, you quickly notice how varied and abundant the pleasures of nature are. I have had a connection with all kinds of animals, many of which have been very important to me.

Almost every memory from my childhood involves some kind of experience of nature: sitting under a tree, watching the nests birds had built, or simply staring at the clouds in the sky. In those moments everything seems to be in perfect harmony, and that peace has stayed with me as a lasting inheritance in life.

When I gladly return to the places of my youth, I always notice again how much they have shaped who I am today. Every step in a naturally beautiful environment, where the shades of light vary and the scents change, is a reminder of how little is needed to be happy and fully present.

I have always been enchanted by the diversity of living creatures. The wave of birdsong in particular has always caught at my heart.
